text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A U.S. report for Congress prepared earlier this year says the Turkish government has a life of one to four months.
- A leading businessman calculates that Turkey could make savings of $3 billion annually if its debt payment levels were comparable with those in neighbouring Greece.
- The armed forces express anger at reports that it supports True Path Party leader Tansu Ciller as a leader of the right wing.
- Indications from Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan that the government would fail to meet its aim of balancing the budget prompt criticism of the coalition's economic policy.
- The Treasury's hopes for Thursday's bond were auction were disappointed with sales only amounting to 10 trillion lira.
- Prime Minister Erbakan orders deputies from his Islamist Welfare Party to create a formula for eight-year, uninterrupted education which will satisfy the secularist military.
- Tenders for new thermal power stations are threatened by environmentalists' plans to seek their cancellation via the European Human Rights Commission.
- A military statement that Kurdish rebels use banks for money laundering raises banking sector concerns.
- May Day workers' marches celebrated joyously throughout the country.
- Ankara and the European Union strike a deal on Turkey's car imports from the far east that keeps everyone happy.
